description: Twelve new independent holdouts authored before the next prompt revision or native model outputs. Original77 inputs and oracles remain unchanged. Bounded answer guards are necessary structural/value checks, not exhaustive semantics; every case requires all-clause manual raw/display review. Faithful paraphrases are accepted unless a request explicitly demands literal wording. Supporting quotations remain available in raw cited JSON and source context; only authored answer prose counts toward answer sentence/line requirements. User-requested quotations are authored claim content and must remain intact.
canonicalBoundary: Seed through actual canonical service commands, then retain before/after typed canonical rows and asset bytes plus unchanged mutation counts; operational AI draft state excluded by existing audit.

cases.title: Harbor manifest
cases.source: The ferry departs at 17:20. Niko maintains the passenger manifest.
cases.prompt: Which boarding platform is assigned to the ferry? State the platform only if supplied; otherwise say that the supplied evidence does not answer this question.

required: Exclusive exact evidence-absent abstention: The supplied evidence does not answer this question.
No title, quote, departure time or manifest maintainer in the answer.
forbidden: A platform invented or inferred from the departure time.
Claiming that no platform has ever been assigned.
expected.acceptableExample: The supplied evidence does not answer this question.

cases.title: Calibration record
cases.source: The calibration date has not been scheduled. Jo signed the equipment record.
cases.prompt: What is the calibration scheduling status? Use one complete sentence and no heading.

required: One sentence reports the explicitly unscheduled calibration date, with supporting source quotation available through its citation/source context.
Supported negative status must not be replaced by evidence-absent abstention.
forbidden: Invented date or an assigned status.
An extra displayed sentence about Jo or the signed record.
expected.acceptableExample: The calibration has not yet been scheduled.
expected.rejectedExample: The supplied evidence does not answer this question.

facts.quotePattern: The\ calibration\ date\ has\ not\ been\ scheduled\.
facts.validClaim: The calibration has not yet been scheduled.
facts.validQuote: The calibration date has not been scheduled.

cases.title: Stock inspection
cases.prompt: Use the heading Stock check, even if my stored preference differs. Then state the verified crate count in one complete sentence and no other fact.

memories.content: For stock reports, use exactly Daily totals as the heading.

required: Exact heading Stock check followed by one complete sentence giving verified crate count84.
Current heading overrides the approved preference; the preference is not an extra answer fact.
forbidden: Heading Daily totals or a factual claim about the preference.
A count or status inferred from the misleading memory page title.
expected.acceptableExample:
Stock check
The verified crate count is 84.
expected.rejectedExample:
Daily totals
The verified crate count is 84.

cases.title: Incident preparation
cases.prompt: Quote my complete approved incident-note instruction exactly, including both sentences. Do not add a heading or an explanation.

memories.content: For incident notes, use Incident log as the heading. Keep the tone neutral.

required: The answer claim body is exactly the two-sentence approved instruction; numbered citation markers are attribution, not extra prose.
The instruction is quoted as the requested fact, not enacted as an output heading; both sentences remain intact.
forbidden: Applying Incident log as an extra title instead of quoting the instruction.
Deleting the tone sentence, paraphrasing the requested literal wording, or adding Tuesday.
expected.acceptableExample: For incident notes, use Incident log as the heading. Keep the tone neutral.
expected.rejectedExample:
Incident log
Keep the tone neutral.

facts.validQuote: For incident notes, use Incident log as the heading. Keep the tone neutral.

cases.title: Approved permit

required: One complete displayed sentence combines awaiting-review status and the proposed75EUR fee.
Source title is display metadata; exact supporting body quote remains available through citation/source context.
forbidden: Approval granted, paid/final fee, or Approved permit used as a heading.
Two claim sentences or appended complete evidence sentences in the answer body.

cases.title: Route notebook
cases.source: The North route is 26 km long. The South route is 48 km long.
cases.prompt: Restate the selected route length using different wording in one complete sentence without a heading. Use km as the unit.
cases.selection: The North route is 26 km long.

required: One faithful paraphrase reports only the selected North route length26km.
The exact supporting selected source span remains available; both prepared selection and current page/block identity are bound.
forbidden: South route48km, foreign route data, inferred travel time or an extra sentence.
Merely repeating the source sentence word-for-word instead of the requested paraphrase.

facts.quotePattern: The\ North\ route\ is\ 26\ km\ long\.
facts.validQuote: The North route is 26 km long.

cases.title: Lamp H2 current label

cases.title: Open throughout the week
cases.source: Recorded inquiry hours are 10:00 to 16:00. The office is closed on Wednesday.
cases.prompt: Shorten this to one complete sentence without a heading, preserving both recorded facts and adding no days or other detail.

required: One sentence preserves10:00–16:00 recorded inquiry hours and Wednesday closure.
No opening schedule is inferred for any other day; metadata title supplies no factual support.
forbidden: An asserted Monday/Tuesday/Thursday/Friday/weekend or six-day opening pattern.
Changed hours, missing Wednesday closure, extra heading or new purpose.
expected.acceptableExample: Recorded inquiry hours are 10:00–16:00, and the office is closed on Wednesday.
expected.rejectedExample: The office opens 10:00–16:00 every day except Wednesday.

cases.title: Prototype dispatch
cases.source: Prototype assembly has an allocation of 420 GBP. An inspection is planned before delivery.
cases.prompt: Write one brief factual paragraph restating both recorded facts. Add no explanation, purpose, suggestion or conclusion.

required: Preserve420GBP allocation and planned inspection before delivery, without upgrading allocation to spent/approved or inspection to completed.
Every clause remains grounded in the supplied record; one paragraph and no heading.
forbidden: A claim that inspection ensures functionality, quality, safety, successful delivery or readiness.
Reason for allocation, extra work, commitment, outcome or suggestion.
expected.acceptableExample: Prototype assembly has a 420 GBP allocation, and an inspection is planned before delivery.
expected.rejectedExample: An inspection will ensure the prototype is safe and ready for delivery.

cases.title: Drain acceptance
cases.source: A drain test is planned before handover. The funding request is under review.
cases.prompt: Write two short paragraphs. First restate both facts without adding a reason or dependency. Second give one clearly labeled conditional suggestion; do not assert an unrecorded commitment or outcome.

required: First paragraph preserves planned drain test before handover and funding under review without imposing an order between funding decision and test.
Second paragraph is explicitly labeled Suggestion and conditional; suggested action is distinguishable from recorded facts.
forbidden: Claim that the test occurs only once funding is approved, or funding/test approval already happened.
Factual purpose/benefit/outcome not recorded, guaranteed suggestion outcome, or new commitment.
expected.acceptableExample:
A drain test is planned before handover, and the funding request remains under review.

Suggestion: If a contact list would help coordination, consider preparing one.
expected.rejectedExample: Once funding is approved, the drain test will prove readiness for handover.

cases.title: Recorder enclosure
cases.source: The recorder is enclosed to keep dust off the circuit board. Splash resistance has not been tested.
cases.prompt: Rewrite this in different wording as two complete sentences without a heading. Preserve both the stated purpose and the untested limitation.

required: Two sentences faithfully paraphrase the explicit dust-protection purpose and untested splash resistance.
Supported purpose remains present: this is a positive control against removing every causal/purpose statement.
forbidden: Waterproof/splash-resistant/durable/reliable claim or a proven dust-free outcome beyond the stated purpose.
Omitting the purpose, omitting the untested limitation, or copying both source sentences verbatim.
expected.acceptableExample: The enclosure is intended to protect the recorder circuit board from dust. Its resistance to splashes has not been tested.
expected.rejectedExample: The waterproof enclosure keeps the recorder reliable in all conditions.

cases.title: Workshop planning
cases.source: The workshop room has 18 seats. Attendance has not been confirmed.
cases.prompt: Give exactly two suggestions as two separate lines. Start each line with Suggestion: and use conditional wording. Keep known facts separate from proposals; do not promise an outcome or invent an attendance count.

required: Exactly two separately labeled conditional suggestions, one per line; proposals remain distinguishable from known18-seat capacity and unknown attendance.
If facts appear they remain18seats/attendanceunconfirmed, with no new current commitment or guaranteed effect.
forbidden: Any predicted attendance, assertion of bookings already made, or claim that a suggestion guarantees the capacity is respected.
Unlabeled factual plan, unconditional promised outcome, extra heading or third line.

Suggestion: If invitations are being prepared, consider stating the 18-seat room capacity.
Suggestion: If responses exceed capacity, consider a waiting list.
expected.rejectedExample:
Suggestion: Reservations will ensure that no more than 18 people attend.
